Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CyberShield Technologies Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss CyberShield Technologies' results for the Q3 FY2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Mia Chen, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Security Officer; Taylor Brooks, VP of Sales; and Casey Nguyen, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report another strong quarter for CyberShield Technologies. Our results reflect the growing importance of cybersecurity in today's digital landscape and our ability to deliver innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers. The market reception to ShieldXDR has been overwhelmingly positive, significantly contributing to its rapid adoption and outsized impact on our growth trajectory.

Our strategy is built on seven key pillars: expanding the number of customers with ARR over $100K, scaling R&D investments as a percentage of revenue, driving expansion within existing large accounts, mitigating the impact of currency fluctuations on revenue, issuing next quarter billings guidance, affirming our full-year revenue and profitability outlook, and detailing the assumptions underlying our guidance.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. We achieved record revenue of $805 million in the Q3 FY2024, representing a 32% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin remained healthy at 82.5%, and we continued to invest in growth initiatives. Operating expenses were $526 million. Net income was $162 million, resulting in earnings per share of $1.14. We are raising our full-year revenue and earnings guidance based on our strong performance to date.

Before we dive deeper, let me walk through some key leading indicators and strategic elements that underscore our momentum. Starting with one of our strongest signals for sustainable growth: the number of customers generating over $100,000 in annual recurring revenue, or ARR. This group highlights our enterprise deployments, where we've landed with core modules like our AI-powered endpoint detection and response platform and expanded into full-stack extended detection and response, secure access service edge, and cloud workload protection.

In Q3 FY2024, we ended with 478 such customers, up 38% year-over-year from 346 and 14% sequentially from 419 in Q2. This surpasses our overall customer growth of 22% YoY, validating our land-and-expand approach. They now drive 68% of total ARR, up from 62% last year, with a net dollar retention of 128% fueled by 25% average upsells, especially in zero-trust network access and managed detection and response add-ons.

Adoption has accelerated with ransomware up 42% globally per Chainalysis. Customers favor converged platforms; 72% of new wins bundled our Nexus XDR with deception technology. This boosted multi-product use by 45% YoY, dropping churn below 2%, far under the 8-10% industry average from KeyBanc surveys.

North America holds 62% or 297 customers, up 12% sequentially via AWS Security Hub and Azure Sentinel ties for Fortune 500 cloud shifts. EMEA jumped 52% YoY to 112, driven by NIS2 and GDPR, with 18 new DAX 40 deals stressing sovereign cloud. APAC grew 41% to 86 customers on Southeast Asia digital pushes and state threats, including top Japanese banks post-pipeline incidents. LatAm doubled to 5% share on Brazil finance growth.

We're intensifying with GenAI Threat Hunter cutting mean-time-to-detect by 65% in pilots, converting 40% to expansions. Fabric interoperability with Splunk and Elastic aims for 20% MSSP co-sell lift. We see 550-570 by year-end, 25-30% FY2025 growth, leveraging CloudSec M&A and $200 million in post-quantum R&D ahead of NIST.

This validates our moat in Gartner's $75 billion TAM.

Shifting to another pillar, our R&D investment remains a cornerstone, as innovation is vital against AI phishing, polymorphic ransomware, and supply chain attacks like SolarWinds. For Q3, R&D was $178 million, or 22.1% of revenue—up 15% YoY in dollars and 180 bps from 20.3% last year. Trailing 12 months at 21.8%, we're at the high end versus Palo Alto's 18.2% or CrowdStrike's 23.5%, balancing aggression with leverage from ShieldXDR scale.

Threats drive this: MITRE shows 40% more living-off-the-land tactics, RaaS like LockBit using ML to shrink dwell times below 24 hours per Mandiant. We put 45% or $80 million into AI/ML, including reinforcement learning slashing false positives 62% versus legacy SIEM.

North America (52% revenue) got $45 million for zero-trust and OT/IoT post-Colonial. EMEA (28%) $32 million for privacy tech like homomorphic encryption amid €2.7 billion fines. APAC (35% YoY growth) $48 million for SASE with 5G against Andariel phishing up 55%.

Flagships: QuantumShield ($25 million) for PQC with 3x faster keys, three patents. AI Sentinel ($35 million) GNNs on 10 petabytes/day cut MTTR to 14 hours for a Fortune 50 bank, lifting NRR 28% to 118%. XDR convergence ($28 million) hit 99.2% detection.

We added 220 engineers, 40% PhDs, for red-teams. At 22.1%, it targets $78 billion SASE TAM, with 60% open-source efficiencies keeping op margins at 32%.

FY2024 averages 22-23%, to 21% FY2025 with GPU clusters. Launches: ShieldXDR 7.0 agentless, SMB MDR, PQC VPN, AI copilot. This powers 125% bookings growth.

Next, expansion within existing large accounts—over $1 million ARR—is a top driver. Our land-and-expand shines with modular XDR, SASE, CWP, deception against APTs like Volt Typhoon or LockBit.

Q2 FY24 DBNR for these was 128%, up 500 bps YoY, 11th quarter over 120%. Expansion revenue $62 million, 42% of ARR growth; 162 of 487 accounts expanded 24.7% average.

By motion: 55% endpoint-to-XDR with MDR; 28% SASE for ZTNA-SWG replacing VPNs; 17% CNAPP for multi-cloud.

North America 68% dollars, 132% DBNR; top-5 bank added $18 million deception. EMEA 145% YoY on NIS2 OT. APAC 115%, NTT bundles.

Customer success QBRs, AI risk scoring (92% accuracy, 1.8x faster expands), Splunk/ServiceNow integrations unlock 30% cross-sells. RPO up 18% QoQ to $1.2 billion.

Expect 125-130% through FY24, $150 million Q3 pipeline on GenAI, 98% retention vs. $4.5 million breach costs.

On currency fluctuations, a key external factor: Q2 FY2024 revenue $248 million, 22% YoY reported but 25% constant currency. FX shaved 300 bps, $5.2 million or 2.1% headwind on 92% gross retention, ARR $980 million up 28% constant.

Mix: 48% Americas, 32% EMEA, 15% APAC, 5% ROW.

EMEA $3.1 million drag (4%), euro up 7% QoQ but GBP down 5%; ARR 32% constant on AWS/Azure ZTA, telco EDR post-MOVEit. APAC $1.4 million (3.8%), JPY tailwind offset CNY/AUD weakness; 35% constant on DPDP data centers. ROW $0.7 million on BRL/MXN; 45% constant MDR.

H1 FY24 $12 million headwind vs. $4 million tailwind prior. Peers similar. Hedged 70% exposures at 1.05 USD/EUR, 0.75 GBP/USD, expanded to JPY/AUD at 65%. Dynamic pricing mitigates 15% APAC erosion; $50 million FY24 edge centers.

Q3 headwind $6-8 million, offset by $2.1 billion RPO up 42% constant, healthcare surge post-Change.

Constant metrics show our durability.

For full-year revenue and profitability outlook: FY2024 revenue $1.28 billion to $1.32 billion, 24-28% YoY from $1.03 billion—up from prior $1.25-1.29 billion midpoint on Q4 enterprise/hyperscaler acceleration. Subscriptions/SaaS 82% mix, $1.05-1.08 billion, 29-33% YoY, NRR 118% on ZTNA/SWG 45% adoption across 4,200+ customers.

Products $185-195 million flat-up 5%; services $105-110 million on MDR/GenAI.

Americas 62% mix, 30% growth on energy/finance. EMEA 24%, 22% on NIS2/Arrow. APAC 14%, 18% tempered by China cycles.

Gross margins 82-83%, +150 bps on SaaS shift. OpEx $825-850 million, 64-65% revenue; S&M 32%, R&D 18% for PQC/ML. Op margins 18-19%, EBITDA $360-380 million (28%), EPS $2.65-2.75 on 142 million shares, $150 million buybacks. FCF >$300 million (23%) for SOAR M&A.

Tailwinds: threats up 35%, 95% net expansion, multi-cloud 60% logos. Risks: budgets, geopolitics, 1% FX shave (60% hedged), uptime.

We're set for record year in agentic AI security.

Finally, next quarter billings guidance for Q4 FY2024 ending June 30th: $285-295 million, 14-18% YoY from $250 million, 8-11% sequential from Q1 $265 million, above 12% peer consensus.

Cloud-native CNAPP >45% mix (from 40%), ACV +25% on CWP/DSPM for Fortune 100 multi-cloud, GenAI misconfigs up 75% per Gartner. EDR 35%, 125% NRR with ZTNA churn <3%.

OT/IoT 10% (from 6%) on Siemens/Schneider, CISA goals, 36-month deals.

Americas 65%, 16% YoY on CMMC $20 million+ primes. EMEA 25%, 20% on GDPR/NIS2 hyperscaler SASE. APAC 10%, 8% despite FX, Japan/Australia sovereign.

AI Fabric on 10 trillion events, 40% faster MTTR per MITRE. RPO to $2.1 billion +22% YoY, 135% ARR. NRR 122-125%, 70% expansions from UEBA.

Risks: rates delaying SMB, China controls, geopolitics accelerating RaaS 30%. Full FY25 billings $1.15-1.18 billion, 15% midpoint in 13.8% CAGR market.

Turning to assumptions underlying FY25 guidance: revenue $1.15-1.18 billion, 27-30% YoY midpoint; op margins 28-30%; EPS $2.85-3.05, building on Q3 32% growth, 115% NRR from ShieldXDR.

Macro: 13.5% cybersecurity CAGR to 2028 per Gartner on RaaS +37%, stable GDP, 100 bps sensitivity for deal delays, $15 million FX drag.

Regions: Americas 58% mix 26% YoY on CMMC/S&P; EMEA 27% 35% NIS2 three eight-figure DAX ZTNA; APAC 15% 42% Singapore/Australia regs, NTT/TCS 25% attach.

Products: 65% XDR bookings, ACV $450K +18% GenAI Hunter 40% faster MTTD on 50 billion events; MDR $180 million +20%; AWS 15% Q3, Azure 12% FY25 ITDR.

Customers: ARR $1.05 billion +29%, NRR 114-116%, 125% expansion offset 8% contract norm; 45 $1M+ deals win 42% vs. CrowdStrike/Palo, 99.9% uptime <5-min SLA, churn <3%.

Ops: gross 82.5% +250 bps XDR 85%; OpEx 52-54%, R&D 18% $150 million AI/QuantumShield; S&M 22% inside/channel 30%; FCF 28%, DSO 65, $50 million buybacks.

Risks: 2% federal haircut, current FX, no CrowdStrike outage impact (+20% PoC). Upside: EMEA regs, 70% Q1 XDR.

This positions us in $200 billion market as breaches average $4.5 million.

Mia Chen: Thank you, Jordan. Our technology roadmap centers on next-generation security leveraging AI, machine learning, and cloud. We're advancing ShieldXDR with GenAI for faster threat detection, post-quantum crypto, and seamless integrations across EDR, CWP, and SOAR to stay ahead of AI-enabled threats and supply chain risks.

Raj Patel: We're committed to top-tier security for customers, vigilantly tracking the threat landscape—from ransomware surges to state-sponsored APTs—and evolving our defenses with zero-trust, autonomous response, and quantum-ready protocols to neutralize emerging vectors.

Taylor Brooks: Demand surges across regions and verticals—financials, critical infrastructure, hyperscalers. Our sales team builds deep customer and partner ties, closing federal CMMC deals, DAX expansions, and APAC channels with NTT/TCS for consistent pipeline conversion.

Casey Nguyen: Marketing builds brand strength and pipeline via digital, PR, events, highlighting ShieldXDR's edge in XDR convergence, cloud-native protection, and AI threat hunting to engage CISOs amid rising breach costs.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: [Instructions for Q&A session]. First question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs.

Emily Carter: Congrats on the quarter. Can you expand on the assumptions behind the FY25 guidance, especially macro and product sensitivities?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Emily. I'll turn this to Jordan for the details.

Jordan Lee: Absolutely, Emily. As I outlined, our FY25 guide assumes robust cybersecurity tailwinds at 13.5% CAGR through 2028 per Gartner, up on geopolitical and AI threats, with RaaS up 37%. Stable GDP, but 100 bps baked for 10-15% cycle extensions. FX $15 million drag embedded. Regionally balanced, 65% XDR bookings at higher ACV, 45 large deals, op efficiencies to 82.5% gross. Conservative on federal, but upside in regs and velocity.

Operator: Next question comes from Mike Thompson with Morgan Stanley.

Mike Thompson: Strong customer metrics—thoughts on R&D allocation driving expansions?

Jordan Lee: Thanks, Mike. Our 22.1% R&D intensity funds AI/ML at 45%, QuantumShield, AI Sentinel cutting MTTR dramatically, and XDR convergence outperforming benchmarks. This directly boosts NRR to 118% and expansions, with regional tailoring for ZTA, privacy, SASE keeping us ahead.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan.

Lisa Chen: How is currency impacting, and billings outlook?

Mia Chen: Lisa, Jordan covered the FX headwind of 300 bps in Q2, hedged 70%, with dynamic pricing and data centers mitigating. For Q4 billings $285-295 million, CNAPP 45%, EDR solid, OT ramping, regions strong despite FX—RPO visibility high at 135% ARR.

Operator: Next question comes from David Ruiz with Barclays.

David Ruiz: Expansion details in large accounts?

Raj Patel: David, large account DBNR 128%, $62 million expansion revenue 42% of growth, endpoint-to-XDR 55%, SASE 28%, via QBRs, AI scoring, integrations. Regional strength, pipeline for 35% ARR organic.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your insightful questions. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and are confident in our ability to deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
